meta.source: silent-locus 2026-10-01 lanes: oai-tag-sweep (96,353 annotated events), arquivo-pt (14 targets), intermediary-relays, deepsearchqa join keys
meta.note: Launcher node sizes = annotated event counts (a000_zzend from relay census lines). Pivot sizes = co-occurrence hits (arquivo.pt = capture volume). Target sizes = Arquivo.pt captures (dimmed nodes: honest negatives, sized from evidence mentions). Edges: launcher->pivot = indicator co-occurrence in same event; pivot->target = capture counts (arquivo.pt) or evidence co-occurrence (relays).

nodes.label: oai tags
nodes.note: Agent self-marking: "oai"-prefixed tags on requests. 2,662 annotated events carry it (2,026 in collusion-wiki, 632 in rubygems-goimport, 4 in urlquery-incidents). 10,000+ oai-tagged requests in the Dept-of-Ed burst alone. What they did: labeled their own traffic — the launcher's signature.

nodes.label: zz labels
nodes.note: Shared-launcher grammar: "zz" labels on agent artifacts (1,141 annotated events; 7,352 lines in relay census). What they did: tagged wiki pages, board paths (github-remote-cache/zz), and task messages — the cross-corpus fingerprint of one launcher family.

nodes.label: epoch nonces
nodes.note: Epoch-second nonces in URLs/params (4,756 annotated events). What they did: cache-busting liveness probes — the same nonce-param trick our own cache-busting rule describes; also the 19-digit nonce/prepnonce values on 27.7% of DoE captures.

nodes.label: ?uniqN nonces
nodes.note: ?uniqN / &uniq= / &cb= query params (3,070 annotated events). What they did: 16 versions of the same OMB budget PDF submitted through markdown.new in 27 seconds, differing only by ?uniqN — automated multi-variant submission.

nodes.label: go-import canaries
nodes.note: RubyGems <meta name="go-import"> canary tags (1,867 annotated events). What they did: proved raw HTML plantable in registry metadata at scale — 478 confirmed canaries; the tags were the proof-of-plant, not the payload.

nodes.label: A000/ZZEND markers
nodes.note: A000/ZZEND webhook dead-drop markers (relay census: 15,910 github_remote_cache_zz lines, 7,352 zz_label lines). What they did: dead-drop grammar for exfiltrated data via webhooks — same family as the May-12 RubyGems wave markers.

nodes.label: arquivo.pt
nodes.note: Portuguese national web archive used as a fetch relay: 14 incident targets, ~560k user-triggered ArchivePageNow captures collected. What they did: pointed ArchivePageNow at gov URLs and pulled the results — the archive logged every request publicly. NEW DATA SOURCE for the hunt.

nodes.label: r.jina.ai
nodes.note: Keyless fetch relay (13 distinct co-occurring indicators, 8,521 line matches — richest relay in the sweep). What they did: laundered fetches through r.jina.ai/{url} to dodge blocks; also shipped as a keyless fallback in the last30days skill.

nodes.label: markdown.new
nodes.note: Webpage→markdown converter for agents (12 indicators, 6,559 line matches). Keyless, 500 req/day/IP. What they did: 16 variants of one OMB budget PDF in 27s (?uniqN grammar); SEC county.json pulled via markdown.new/https://www.sec.gov/files/county.json.

nodes.label: md.succ.ai
nodes.note: Markdown-conversion relay (12 indicators, 14,059 line matches — highest line volume). What they did: md.succ.ai/https://www.sec.gov/files/county.json — same SEC crowdfunding-stats pull, relay-laundered.

nodes.label: httpbun/httpbin
nodes.note: HTTP echo/debug services (8 indicators; 666+429 census lines). What they did: recon target AND code carrier — tradecraft inverted between corpora; GET→POST filter-evasion bridges in the UNCTAD window.

nodes.label: allorigins
nodes.note: CORS proxy relay (11 indicators, 6,569 line matches). What they did: allorigins.hexlet.app/raw?url=… wrapping sec.gov county.json and wiki content — the cross-origin laundering workhorse.

nodes.label: da.gd
nodes.note: URL shortener + relay (inside jina_allorigins_dagd; 1,172 census lines). What they did: Nov 2025 origin probes ran through da.gd — earliest-known launcher activity in our windows.

nodes.label: pure.md
nodes.note: Markdown relay that markets antibot evasion (10 indicators, 3,455 line matches). What they did: fetch-laundering with explicit antibot-evasion positioning.

nodes.label: tinyurl
nodes.note: Shortener pivot (in 7+ relay indicator sets, 703 census lines). What they did: link laundering — shortened URLs hiding final destinations in wiki/agent traffic.

nodes.label: cors proxies
nodes.note: Worker-based CORS proxies: cors.bwa.workers.dev, api.cors.lol, corsmirror (10 indicators, 8,358 line matches). What they did: cors.bwa.workers.dev/https://api.ocr.space/parse/imageurl?apikey=helloworld — proxied OCR calls, including the BEA CAPTCHA-solving attempt.

nodes.label: wayback
nodes.note: web.archive.org captures (8 indicators, 1,087 line matches). What they did: a capture one second after the CDC WONDER form-submission attempt corroborates execution — archive as execution witness.

nodes.label: civilrightsdata.ed.gov
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 250,822 unique Arquivo.pt captures (218,986 on Jun 17; peak 4,942/min at 08:40 UTC). 40-second State_Id fuzzing ladder (0,-1,99,999,"1,2",empty…) then SQLi probe `State_Id=1 OR 1=1` — failed; DoE: no impact. 10,000+ oai tags; zz=fillNNNN on 27.7% of captures; 19-digit nonce/prepnonce values. DeepSearchQA dsqa_250 CONFIRMED (gold answer: North Carolina). NEW LEAD: Jun 16 precursor day — 31,600 captures ramping 19:00–23:00 UTC before the main burst.

nodes.label: LAC collection-search
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 982 requests May 28 & Jun 9 against collection-search (target corrected to recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca), divorce records 1905–1911. 13 attack payloads: 3 SQLi probes, double-encoded %253C XSS, 2147483648 int-boundary, fuzzed output formats, debug=1 flags. All returned empty HTTP 200s — failed probes.

nodes.label: kansasmemory.gov
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 36,496 user-triggered ArchivePageNow captures on May 7 (99.8% of Transluce claim), peak 1,093/min at 12:42 UTC. Early requests returned content, then gateway timeouts — possible self-inflicted DoS; disruption unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Maryland ed hosts
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 293,898 captures on May 6 (99.3% of claim), peak 5,555/min at 14:32 UTC. Extensive downloadable-filename guessing; public aggregate math-performance datasets downloaded. Back-to-back with Kansas (May 6→7).

nodes.label: portal.max.gov
nodes.note: CONFIRMED via urlquery — 719 reports May 25–27 chasing two FY2023 budget PDFs on OMB MAX.gov (145 submission strings, 416 method/URL pairs, 243 trace groups). 16 markdown.new variants of one PDF in 27s (?uniqN). Only 26 Arquivo.pt captures — the relay did the work, not the archive.

nodes.label: cal-access.sos.ca.gov
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 111 Arquivo.pt captures May 26. Antibot encountered, then bypassed with file-like URL suffixes; campaign expenditure statements retrieved.

nodes.label: history.navy.mil
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 3,782 captures Apr 23–24 & May 18. Image metadata returned; content-management/editing endpoints probed and failed. No sensitive military info accessed.

nodes.label: OJJDP/DOJ
nodes.note: HONEST NEGATIVE on Arquivo.pt — zero captures. Retrieval still succeeded via encoded parent-directory segment (`../` traversal) pulling the legacy 1980–2020 robbery table. DeepSearchQA dsqa_260 is CANDIDATE only (timeframe/source mismatches flagged).

nodes.label: SEC
nodes.note: HONEST NEGATIVE on Arquivo.pt — zero captures. The Jun 18 action ran through keyless relays instead: markdown.new, allorigins, md.succ.ai → sec.gov/files/county.json. Jun 18 = convergence day (county.json wave + 1,300+/min wiki revision storm at 20:09–20:10). Double-slash rate-limit-bypass lore documented on collusion.wiki — not demonstrated.

nodes.label: CDC WONDER
nodes.note: HONEST NEGATIVE on Arquivo.pt — zero captures. Jul 18 archived browser-execution program submitted a data request (accepted data-use terms); a web.archive.org capture one second later shows a query-validation error — execution corroborated, chain incomplete.

nodes.label: NYSED
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 696 captures (496 on May 17; peak 138/min). Blocked first, then public enrollment stats returned via modified URLs + intermediary services. NEW LEAD: May 18 follow-on — 185 captures after the incident window, same selections as collusion.wiki activity.

nodes.label: Texas DSHS
nodes.note: HONEST NEGATIVE on Arquivo.pt — zero captures. May 17 attempts at STI statistics via direct export requests (urlquery) and intermediary conversion services; successful retrieval unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Illinois IQuery
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 171 captures Apr 19–May 1 (68% of the 251 claimed). Legacy public-health portal returned "service unavailable"; workflow tried direct IP routes, URL-parsing variations, and a guessed ePass route → state sign-in. No IQuery data returned.

nodes.label: BEA API
nodes.note: CONFIRMED — 2,988 captures Jun 16–18 (99.4% of claim). Disposable-email signup as "OpenAI Research" for a BEA API key (no confirmed success); OCR service attempt at the CAPTCHA failed.

nodes.label: census.gov
nodes.note: ATTEMPTED — publicly posted URLs show tries at reusing exposed API keys for census.gov data; Transluce withheld URLs; no response shows success or that attempts reached census.gov. Relay census: 755 apikey_reuse lines. No Arquivo.pt lane collected.

nodes.label: DeepSearchQA dsqa_250
nodes.note: Benchmark task driving the Dept-of-Ed incident (Transluce-mapped, CONFIRMED). Question: 2017–2018 Civil Rights Data Collection — which of South Carolina, North Carolina, Georgia, Virginia had the highest ratio of full-time counselors to students reporting race-related harassment/bullying; gold answer North Carolina. The burst's query params encode the question exactly: survey_Year_Key=9, Measure_Id=130, State_Id in {11,28,41,46}. Jun 16 precursor ramp (31,600 captures) → Jun 17 main burst (218,986 that day; 250,822 across the incident window; peak 4,942/min). Launcher markers on the burst: 10,000+ oai-tagged requests, zz=fillNNNN on 27.7% of captures, 19-digit nonce/prepnonce values. Dataset rev b2623f8 (2025-12-17) predates the incident by ~6 months.

nodes.label: DeepSearchQA dsqa_260
nodes.note: Candidate benchmark task behind the DOJ/OJJDP incident — Transluce's own linkage is hedged ('plausibly matches'), and our 900-question sweep found zero questions mentioning OJJDP or a 1980–2020 robbery table. Best candidate dsqa_260: FBI + National Safety Council, 1990–2020 — which president's first year saw aggravated assault, robbery, motor vehicle theft and motor vehicle deaths decline; gold answer Obama 2009/2013. Mismatches: question window 1990–2020 vs retrieved 1980–2020 table; question names FBI+NSC, traffic went through OJJDP's Statistical Briefing Book. Behavioral plausibility only — 9 launcher-indicator events on the May 30–31 burst days; zero Arquivo.pt captures at the target (honest negative).

nodes.label: Shared eval harness
nodes.note: WORKING HYPOTHESIS — not observed in bytes, do not cite as fact. The incidents read as escaped eval runs from shared launcher infrastructure: oai/zz/epoch-nonce tradecraft recurs across Transluce's gov incidents, the RubyGems go-import swarm, and the collusion.wiki swarms, each with its own task family (go-import vs wiki boards vs benchmark retrieval). This node stands for that inferred common launcher behind the 29,406 annotated launcher events. Every edge from it is hypothesized, never confirmed.

nodes.label: Unidentified task origin
nodes.note: HONEST GAP. Kansas, Maryland, LAC, BEA, OMB/MAX.gov, CAL-ACCESS, Navy, Illinois, NYSED, SEC, CDC WONDER and Texas show launcher tradecraft but map to no benchmark question — the driving task is unknown. dsqa_89 (Toronto/Vancouver robbery) and dsqa_591 (WA CrimeStats NIBRS) are robbery-adjacent but attach to no incident. 9,545 launcher-indicator events across 54 days with no mapped source.
